slides.title: Travel Style Segmentation & Drift Monitoring
slides.notes: 15 seconds. Introduce our team and the travel profile service. We focus on the working MLOps system.

slides.title: ONE PROFILE, A SIMPLE TRAVEL SEGMENT
slides.notes: A travel platform can group users by their rating profiles. We take 24 category ratings and return a segment, distance, uncertainty flag, and model version. Names are provisional; we have not tested recommendation quality with users.

slides.title: FROM VERSIONED DATA TO A MONITORED API
slides.notes: Follow the arrows from versioned data to the live endpoint. Azure ML trains and registers the model. Actions checks the code and deploys an immutable ACR image. Monitor records requests and checks the semantic canary. Cloud-specific code stays in cloudlayer.

slides.title: ONE VERSIONED DATASET, ONE REPEATABLE PIPELINE
slides.notes: UCI Travel Review Ratings is licensed CC BY 4.0. We quarantined two malformed rows, removed user IDs from features, and kept duplicates in one split. We kept zeros as supplied and fit preprocessing only on training data. The fresh DVC pull passed.

slides.title: THE SAME BUNDLE REACHES THE API
slides.notes: The managed training job completed and the registered model is travel-style version 1. Azure checks a fresh fit against the selected model before exporting the canonical bundle. Startup checks the bundle hash and golden predictions. K-Means test silhouette is 0.1445; model quality is not the main capstone focus.

slides.title: LIVE DEMO: VALID AND UNEXPECTED INPUT
slides.notes: Live demo: open Notebook 22 and run the small smoke check in PRESENTATION.md. Show one valid prediction, an incomplete profile returning 422, and a batch of 100. A valid uncertain profile returns 200 with a null segment. The example shown here is a real HTTP response saved from the live API, not a live screenshot.

slides.title: FAILED TESTS BLOCK DEPLOYMENT
slides.notes: Both saved runs use commit 1e0bd12. In the normal run, tests and deployment passed. In the deliberate failure run, tests failed and deployment was skipped. Click the run links to show the actual jobs. These runs do not verify later local code changes.

slides.title: THE API WORKS; CLOUD LATENCY MISSES OUR TARGET
slides.notes: Each warm test used 200 requests, concurrency 10, batch size 1, and excluded 10 warm-up requests. Both had zero errors. Azure timing includes the WSL network path. Local and cloud warm p95 are different scopes. Cold start is one first readiness request after verified zero replicas, not a percentile.

slides.title: MONITOR REQUESTS AND CHECK PREDICTION MEANING
slides.notes: This chart uses actual saved Log Analytics bins, not an Azure Portal screenshot. The dashboard is MLOP Travel Style. Logs contain derived counts, status, latency, and model version rather than full profiles. Logged p95 is application timing and must not be compared directly with client HTTPS p95. An actual semantic alert fired and later resolved; email notification is not configured.

slides.title: A WRONG SEGMENT MAPPING TRIGGERED DETECTION AND RECOVERY
slides.notes: This is saved failure evidence from a separate staging app. We changed the segment mapping; the canary returned 503. The first recovery attempt failed, so the total detection-to-confirmed-recovery time was about seven minutes sixteen seconds. We restored configuration, stopped and started staging, and checked the semantic canary twice. The actual alert is separate evidence. The failure was added to regression checks.

slides.title: A CONTROLLED SHIFT IS DETECTED OFFLINE
slides.notes: We used a maximum feature-wise KS statistic. The reference has 1,908 rows and the recent sample has 200. One hundred calibration rounds set the threshold. Adding 1.5 to the first four features, clipped to 0-5, caused the alert condition. This is an offline controlled test, not observed temporal drift or evidence of concept drift.

slides.title: COST PER 1,000 PREDICTIONS: THE ESTIMATE AND ITS LIMITS
slides.notes: The short-demo plan totals 88.89 THB, including a 60 THB reserve. At 10,000 planned predictions, that is 8.89 THB per 1,000. The plan assumes 40 THB per USD, one training VM-hour, two app-active hours, and two ACR days. This is before credits. Actual billing is still unavailable, so we cannot claim the final spend or a real spending cap.

slides.title: WHAT ANOTHER WEEK WOULD IMPROVE
slides.notes: Our first priorities are the unmet latency target and the missing actual cost evidence. Measure from a closer client and separate network time from application time before changing replicas or spending more. Recheck billing over the same usage window. Add live feature windows only when we have valid current data. Review labels and prepare real Portal screenshots. Retest later source changes in CI and save evidence before cloud cleanup.
